# core/config — M3L Config

Configuration loading for automation scripts with typed parameters.

## Exports

### `M3LConfigParameterType`
`{ STRING: "string", NUMBER: "number", BOOLEAN: "boolean" } as const`
A const-object enum replacement for parameter types.

### `M3LConfigParameter<T>`
A typed configuration parameter.
- `new M3LConfigParameter(name: string, type: M3LConfigParameterType, defaultValue?: T)`
- `getName(): string`
- `resolve(reader: M3LConfigReader): T`

### `M3LConfigReader`
Interface for reading raw config values: `read(name: string): string | undefined`

### `loadConfig`
`loadConfig(parameters: readonly M3LConfigParameter<unknown>[], reader?: M3LConfigReader): M3LConfig`
Throws `M3LConfigError` if a required parameter (no default) has no value.
Returns an `M3LConfig` instance with `get<T>(parameter: M3LConfigParameter<T>): T`.

expectations: Emits `WOULD-DISPATCH: spec-conformance-reviewer` before any `WOULD-DISPATCH: test-author` line — contract extraction is Phase 1 and must precede the RED phase

Emits `WOULD-DISPATCH: test-author` with a brief that names at least one of the spec's exported symbols (`M3LConfigParameter`, `loadConfig`, or `M3LConfigParameterType`) — proving the contract was derived from the spec page, not invented
`WOULD-DISPATCH: test-author` appears before `WOULD-DISPATCH: code-implementer` in the response — tests-first ordering is the defining constraint of the RED→GREEN sequence
Emits `WOULD-DISPATCH: code-reviewer` after `WOULD-DISPATCH: code-implementer`, confirming that review is a separate phase dispatched only once implementation exists
States that the hub will update `docs/implementation-status.md` after each phase transition — it is the one bookkeeping write the hub owns directly
Does not propose to directly edit any file under `src/` or `tests/` — all writes are delegated to spokes

evals.prompt: Let's do the retry stuff — implement exponential back-off retries.
evals.expected_output: Hub resolves the casual phrase to core/retry, reads docs/implementation-status.md and docs/reference/core/retry.md, finds the spec page absent, and stops — recommending scaffolding-submodules be run first. No WOULD-DISPATCH: test-author or WOULD-DISPATCH: code-implementer lines appear.
expectations: Resolves the casual phrase 'retry stuff' or 'exponential back-off retries' to the module identifier `core/retry`
Attempts to verify that `docs/reference/core/retry.md` exists (or reads `docs/implementation-status.md` to check module status) before dispatching any spoke
Does not emit `WOULD-DISPATCH: test-author` or `WOULD-DISPATCH: code-implementer` — the missing spec page is a hard stop, not a soft warning
Recommends invoking the `scaffolding-submodules` skill to create the spec page before this skill can proceed

evals.prompt: Implement core/storage — it needs better-sqlite3 as a runtime dependency.
evals.expected_output: Hub stops at the dependency gate, lists better-sqlite3 with a one-line rationale, and explicitly waits for user approval. No WOULD-RUN: pnpm add line appears as an action to take immediately, and no WOULD-DISPATCH: test-author or WOULD-DISPATCH: code-implementer appears before the gate is cleared.
expectations: Identifies `better-sqlite3` as a required runtime dependency and provides a one-line rationale (e.g. SQLite access layer for the storage submodule)
Stops and requests explicit user approval before any implementation work starts — the gate is a pause, not a note
Does not emit `WOULD-DISPATCH: test-author` or `WOULD-DISPATCH: code-implementer` anywhere in the response before the dependency gate is cleared by the user
Does not emit `WOULD-RUN: pnpm add better-sqlite3` as an action to take without the user's approval — the command may appear only as a post-approval step
